podcast.body: A double-live album recorded in October 1974, capturing performances from the ambitious "Diamond Dogs" tour. This release contributed to Bowie's incredible output of five studio albums and one live record within a span of just two years and ten months. "That fall, October 1974, a double-live album was taken from the tour that made for five studio albums and one live record in just two years and ten months."

podcast.body: Released in 1974, this concert album showcased Bowie's R&B allusions, cracking the Billboard Top 10. Both the album cover photo, depicting Bowie in a silky suit, and the live arrangements, with songs like "Rock and Roll Suicide" rearranged to sound like Otis Redding, presented Bowie fully in his "Soulman" persona, crooning like an R&B artist. "These R&B allusions persisted on Boey's other major LP release of 1974, the concert album David Live. It too cracked the Billboard Top 10, and from the photo on the album cover to the live arrangements, Boey was giving Soulman, a screening in a silky suit and vocalizing like an R&B crooner."
